name: Question 9
problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}7-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vector $v$ and the rotation-scaling matrix $C$ shown above. Given that $v$ is an eigenvector of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\text{i},$ find a matrix $P$ such that $A=PC{P}^{-1}.$
worked_solution:
Recall that for any $2\times 2$ real matrix $A$ with complex eigenvalues, we have $A=PC{P}^{-1},$ where 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}],
$$

and $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the complex eigenvalue  $\lambda .$

First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}(\lambda ) & \text{Im}(\lambda ) \\ -\text{Im}(\lambda ) & \text{Re}(\lambda )\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]=C.
$$

Next, we can find the real and imaginary parts of our eigenvector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}7-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now construct $P:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ \text{Re}(v) & \text{Im}(v) \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
